A vertical 9:16 overhead insert shot, like a 1970s British espionage film: a stiff buff government envelope has just dropped onto a scuffed green leather desk top in a Whitehall office, still sliding, a corner lifting. Printed at the top: "O.H.M.S." beside a small invented crest of a crowned key between two herons, and "EXPORT LICENCE" in typewriter capitals. Across the middle, a slightly crooked red rubber stamp in heavy block capitals reads exactly "APPROVED BY THE CONSERVATIVE PARTY", the ink pooling at one edge. A brass banker's lamp throws warm tungsten light from the left; a cold grey window spills blue from the right. Kodak 35mm film stock, 40mm lens, fine grain, a ring stain from a teacup. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 linocut print in two inks only, black and a hot vermilion red, on off-white rough rag paper with visible gouge marks and slightly uneven ink. Seen from directly above: a large envelope falling flat onto a desk, carved speed lines behind it, a single bare hand in a shirt cuff just letting go at the top edge. The envelope carries a small carved crest of a crowned key between two herons and the words "O.H.M.S.". Stamped across it in red, in chunky carved block letters, exactly "APPROVED BY THE CONSERVATIVE PARTY". The desk grain is cut as bold parallel lines; a fountain pen and a blotter sit beside it. Misregistration of the red by a few millimetres, like a hand-pulled print. Thanks.
